senses.gloss: pr. n. pl.(b. h. תַּדְמֹר)Tadmor (Tarmod) = Palmyra, in an oasis of the Syrian desert.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Kings 9:18">Targ. I Kings IX, 18</cite>; <cite ref="II Chronicles 8:4">II Chr. VIII, 4</cite> (ed. Lag. <he>תדמר</he>).—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 1:6:5">Y. Yeb. I, 3ᵃ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 4:6:3">Y. Kidd. IV, 65ᵈ</cite> top <he>גירי ת׳</he> proselytes from T.; <cite ref="Niddah 56b:35">Nidd. 56ᵇ</cite> <he>מקבלין גרים מתר׳</he> we may admit proselytes from Tarmod; <cite ref="Yevamot 16b:1">Yeb. 16ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Yevamot 17a:8">Ib. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>פסולי דת׳</he> those of blemished descent from T.
<cite ref="Yevamot 17a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>היינו ת׳ היינו תַּמּוֹד</he> Tarmod and Tammod are the same.
<cite ref="Yevamot 17a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>משאול לת׳</he> from hell to T., v. <cite ref="C01092"><he>גַּנְדַּר</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 56:11">Gen. R., s. 56</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 22:17">Gen. XXII, 17</cite>) <he>זו ת׳ אשריו … של ת׳ וכ׳</he> ‘the gate of its enemies’, that is T.; happy he who sees the downfall of T., which was a partner &c., v. <cite ref="U00585"><he>שׁוּתָּף</he></cite>; Y. Taan. IV, 69ᵇ <he>תר׳</he>; <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2:4">Lam. R. to II, 2</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 102:2">Yalk. Gen. 102</cite>; a. e.—Denom. h. <he>תַּדְמוּרִי</he>, <cite ref="V01013"><he>תַּרְמוּדִי</he></cite>; pl. <he>תַּדְמוּרִים</he>, <he>תַּדְמוּרִיִּים</he>, <he>תַּדְמוּרִיִּין</he>, <cite ref="V01013"><he>תַּרְמוּדִ׳</he></cite>. Y. Yeb. l. c.; Bab.
Sabb. 31ᵃ; Ab. d’R. N. ch. XV; a. e.—Fem. תַּדְמוּרִית.
Tosef. Naz. IV, 10 ed. Zuck. (Var. תודמרית, corr. acc.).—Ch. תַּדְמוּרָאָה, תַּרְמוּדָ׳; pl. תַּדְמוּרָאֵי, תַּרְמוּדָ׳.
<cite ref="Shabbat 21b">Sabb. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>תרמוד׳</he> Palmyreans, dealers in kindling material.
